about: The masters of the playable races (order 96, D-193): linked, never copied. Their sheets (level, capabilities, titles, skills, items, story) are data/power.json's masters, which A.POWER reads; this file adds only what a full profile needs that those sheets lack: the class road (data/classes.json, step by step from a first class), the arts readied (names of their own active skills), a temper and traits, goals and grudges A.WHY can read, the home's name and whether it is known, and the secret. Validated by tools/lint-figures.mjs.

category.name: Masters of the Peoples
category.note: The strongest of the giants, the dwarves, the elves and the orcs: each the best of a people, and very few on the whole continent stand near them.

goals.why: to keep the ice road open, so his people are never shut in the fells again
to see a son of his on the throne under Jotunhall

grudges.why: the dwarves of Irondeep hold the passes his people need

story: The eldest giant still on a throne, who broke the ice road open with his own maul when the fells were shut by a winter that lasted nine years.
He is dying of his years, slowly. Two of his sons are already counting the spears of the other.

goals.why: that the Ninth Gate of Irondeep is never opened from below again

grudges.why: the Ash-Crowned has burned three dwarf halls for one stolen scale

story: The warden of the Ninth Gate of Irondeep, who held it alone for a night and a day when something came up out of the deep roads.
What came up the deep roads was not killed. It went back down, and the gate has been knocked on from below every winter since.

goals.why: one more bout with the Sword Saint before one of them dies

grudges.why: the Archdemon sang at his sister's funeral and took her voice

story: The eldest blade of the elves of Evenglade, who has never once hurried a cut in nine hundred years. He fought the Sword Saint once, when both were younger, and lost by a hair.
He let the Saint win. He has wondered every day since whether he had to.

goals.why: every clan of the Grass Sea under one khan, and that khan himself
the iron of the dwarves, by trade or by taking

grudges.why: the giants laughed at his father's embassy

story: The Skull-Khan of Urgol, who ate at the Iron Feast and rose from it khan of nine clans. He wears the skulls of the eight khans who did not.
One of the eight is still alive, in a pit under Urgol. The khan visits him on feast days and asks him how it feels to lose.
